# Adjudication Task — Chapter 430

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃430화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|나도 모르게 눈꺼풀이 파르르 떨렸다.
  6|
  7|‘……이게 왜 여기에.’
  8|
  9|똑똑히 기억하고 있다.
 10|
 11|서천마군에 의해 몇 번이나 죽을 위기를 넘겨야 했던 사천혈사(四川血史)가 마무리된 직후, 청성파와 아미파 장문인의 인도하에 향했던 어느 이름 모를 절벽의 동굴.
 12|
 13|기문진 뒤에 숨겨져 있던 공간은 실로 광활했고, 그 중심부에는 거대한 진법(陳法)이 새겨져 있었다.
 14|
 15|지금 내가 들고 있는 종이에 컬러로 프린트된, 기이한 문양과 기호로 가득한 진법이.
 16|
 17|하지만…… 청성과 아미의 장문인들이 이동진(異動陳)이라 이름 붙였던 그것을 더 이상 진법이라고 부를 수 있을까?
 18|
 19|나는 다급히 매직 존슨을 향해 종이를 들이밀었다.
 20|
 21|“존슨. 이거, 이거 뭐예요?”
 22|
 23|「어, 어?」
 24|
 25|“이게 왜…… 아니, 도대체 어디서 난 겁니까?”
 26|
 27|갑작스러운 내 반응에 당황한 매직 존슨이 얼떨떨한 표정으로 대꾸했다.
 28|
 29|「아크 리치가 본거지로 삼았던 도시에서 발견한 마법진이야.」
 30|
 31|“마법진이요?”
 32|
 33|「응, 마법진. 안 그래도 이것 때문에 한창 연구 중이었는데…… 왜 그래, 진? 혹시 어디서 본 적 있어?」
 34|
 35|“다른 것도 있어요?”
 36|
 37|「물론이지. 네가 들어오기 전까지 보고 있던 종이들이 전부 그것과 관련된 내용이니까.」
 38|
 39|“네?”
 40|
 41|그럼 책상 위에 쌓여 있던 그게 전부?
 42|
 43|나는 바닥에 널브러진 수십여 장의 종이를 바라보았다.
 44|
 45|“자, 잠깐만 실례할게요.”
 46|
 47|「진, 진?」
 48|
 49|“드디어 미쳐 버린 것인가. 안타깝구나, 못생기고 간악한 인간이여.”
 50|
 51|당황한 매직 존슨의 부름과 스켈레톤 킹의 헛소리는 안중에도 없었다.
 52|
 53|나는 입을 꾹 다문 채 프린트된 종이 뭉치를 빠르게 훑어 나갔다.
 54|
 55|수십 장의 종이에는 각각의 문양과 기호가 새겨져 있었고, 그 모든 것을 다 살펴본 후 한 가지 사실을 깨달을 수 있었다.
 56|
 57|‘이건…….’
 58|
 59|틀림없다. 배치와 방향이 다를 뿐, 기이한 문양과 기호는 무림에서 본 그것과 동일했다.
 60|
 61|그리고 이 종이들을 퍼즐처럼 한데 모으면 하나의 거대한 마법진이 완성된다는 것도.
 62|
 63|‘이게 무슨 개 같은 상황이지?’
 64|
 65|쇠망치로 뒤통수를 한 대 얻어맞은 기분이다.
 66|
 67|말없이 종이들을 노려보던 내가 입을 연 것은 그로부터 상당한 시간이 흐른 뒤였다.
 68|
 69|“이거, 아크 리치의 본거지에서 발견한 거라고 하셨죠?”
 70|
 71|어느새 시가를 문 매직 존슨을 바라보며 묻자, 그가 연기를 뿜으며 대답했다.
 72|
 73|「그래. 나도 처음에는 그런 게 있는 줄 몰랐는데, 조사단 투입 직후에 발견된 것 같아. 이틀째에 연합군을 통해서 전달받았지.」
 74|
 75|“전달받았다는 건…….”
 76|
 77|「내게 자문을 구했거든. 저쪽에서도 정확히 어떤 기능의 마법진인지 파악하지 못한 거지. 아마 나 말고 다른 두 명에게도 연락이 갔을걸?」
 78|
 79|다른 두 명이란 매직 존슨을 제외한 다른 대마도사들일 것이다. 그들이야말로 현존하는 최고의 마법사들이자, 진정한 전문가들이니까.
 80|
 81|그리고 그 말은 이 마법진이 지금껏 드러난 적 없는 새로운 종류의 것이라는 뜻이기도 했다.
 82|
 83|“그래서, 연구하신 결과는 나왔습니까?”
 84|
 85|「아직 정확한 건 아니지만, 마법진의 용도에 대해서는 갈피를 잡았지.」
 86|
 87|“용도요?”
 88|
 89|「응. 다행히 그쪽에 대해 제법 잘 아는 친구가 하나 있었거든.」
 90|
 91|그게 누구냐고 물어보려던 순간, 한 사람이 오만한 목소리로 불쑥 끼어들었다.
 92|
 93|“바로 이 몸이시지. 미국 조지아주 애틀랜타에서 출생한 우주 대존잘 미남. 이름하여 스톤-킹.”
 94|
 95|맞다. 왜 저놈을 잊고 있었지?
 96|
 97|마계 토박이에 네임드 몬스터씩이나 되는 놈이니 뭔가를 알고 있을 것이 분명하다.
 98|
 99|나는 헛소리를 늘어놓는 스켈레톤 킹을 다그쳤다.
100|
101|“개소리하지 말고 아는 거나 빨리 털어놔.”
102|
103|“앞으로 미스터 킹이라고 부른다면 생각해 보지.”
104|
105|“미스터 킹 같은 소리 하고 자빠졌네, 낑깡 같은 새끼가.”
106|
107|“퍽킹 코리안.”
108|
109|“시벌 놈이.”
110|
111|“워어, 워어!”
112|
113|내가 손을 쳐들자 자신도 모르게 후다닥 물러난 스켈레톤 킹이 황급히 외쳤다.
114|
115|“알았다! 알았다고!”
116|
117|“말해, 인마.”
118|
119|경계 어린 눈빛으로 나를 바라본 스켈레톤 킹이 입을 열었다.
120|
121|“생명력 흡수를 위한 마법진인 것 같다.”
122|
123|“생명력 흡수?”
124|
125|“그래. 아크 리치가 다른 인간들의 기운을 흡수하여 힘을 축적하는 용도로 쓴 것 같더군. 그렇게 끌어모은 마력이 있으니 수많은 몬스터 군단을 제어하고 게이트를 열 수 있었던 거겠지.”
126|
127|중국은 광활한 대륙이다.
128|
129|대격변으로 엄청난 사상자를 냈음에도 여전히 전 세계 인구의 5분지 1에 해당하는 사람들이 남아 있다.
130|
131|그리고 그중 쓰촨성에 거주하는 인구는 ‘공식 통계로만’ 약 8천만 명.
132|
133|이번 몬스터 웨이브가 낳은 사상자는 수백만에 달하고, 아직 공식 집계되지 않은 이들까지 더한다면 실로 어마어마한 숫자로 불어난다.
134|
135|‘그리고 그들 중 상당수의 목숨이 마력을 위한 희생양이 되었겠지. 놈이 벌였던 짓의 규모를 생각하면 어느 정도 아귀가 맞아떨어져.’
136|
137|입술을 질끈 깨문 나는 스켈레톤 킹을 향해 재차 물었다.
138|
139|“확실한 거야?”
140|
141|“개인적인 유추일 뿐, 장담은 못 한다.”
142|
143|“어째서?”
144|
145|스켈레톤 킹이 혀를 찼다.
146|
147|“간악한 인간이여. 너는 다른 인간들이 사용하는 마법진을 보는 것만으로도 판단할 수 있나?”
148|
149|“그건…….”
150|
151|“당연히 모르겠지. 이 몸도 마찬가지다. 주어진 능력에 따라 병사들을 일으켜 세우고 이끌 수는 있어도, 이와 같은 흑마법을 부리지는 못해.”
152|
153|젠장. 전부 맞는 말이다.
154|
155|헌터와 몬스터를 각자의 특성에 따라 분류하는 것처럼, 스켈레톤 킹도 딱 그만큼의 능력을 지니고 있을 뿐이다.
156|
157|기대했던 대답이 나오지 않자 나도 모르게 힘이 빠졌지만, 아직 중요한 질문이 남아 있었다.
158|
159|“그럼 생명력 흡수 마법진인 건 어떻게 짐작한 거지? 혹시 이런 문양이나 기호들은 몬스터만 알아볼 수 있는 건가?”
160|
161|스켈레톤 킹이 이 기이한 문양과 기호를 알고 있다면, 녀석에게서 그것들이 의미하는 바를 배울 수 있다면 무림에서 본 진법의 정체도 명확하게 밝혀 낼 수 있다.
162|
163|기대를 담아 스켈레톤 킹을 바라본 나는, 잠시 후 흘러나온 대답에 맥이 탁 풀렸다.
164|
165|“저것들이 무엇을 뜻하는지는 모른다. 마법진의 용도는 이 몸이 언데드라 가능했던 일이었고.”
166|
167|스켈레톤 킹이 매직 존슨을 가리키며 말을 이었다.
168|
169|“처음 이런 종이로 봤을 때는 잘 몰랐지만, 저 고마운 인간과 함께 현장에 가 보니 확실히 느껴지더군. 나조차도 짐작할 수 없는 수많은 죽음의 냄새가 느껴졌었다. 그때 처음으로 알게 되었지.”
170|
171|“아…….”
172|
173|실망감을 감출 수 없었다.
174|
175|대마도사인 매직 존슨은 물론이고 네임드 몬스터인 스켈레톤 킹조차 알 수 없다면, 당장 저 문양과 기호의 뜻을 알아내는 건 불가능에 가깝다는 뜻이니까.
176|
177|‘제기랄.’
178|
179|도대체 무슨 일이 벌어지고 있는 거지?
180|
181|동굴 중심부에 새겨져 있던 진법, 이번에 발견된 마법진에서 나타난 문양과 기호, 그리고 혈주와 서천마군과의 전투에서 목격한 괴이한 현상들…….
182|
183|머릿속에 스치는 어떤 불길한 생각을, 마음 깊은 곳에서 애써 부정한다.
184|
185|그럴 리가 없다고. 있을 수 없는 일이라고.
186|
187|이건 우연일까. 아니면 운명일까.
188|
189|운명이라면 난데없이 나타난 이 연결 고리가 의미하는 것은 무엇일까.
190|
191|한참 동안 말없이 룸 안을 서성이던 나는 불쑥 입을 열었다.
192|
193|“직접 가 봐야겠어.”
194|
195|「응?」
196|
197|“음?”
198|
199|“존슨. 저 녀석이 가 봤다는 그 현장, 저도 가 볼 수 있죠?”
200|
201|잠시 고민하던 매직 존슨이 고개를 끄덕였다.
202|
203|「기밀이긴 하지만…… 진이라면 충분히 가능하지. 단, 모습을 보이는 건 우리 둘뿐이야. 저 친구는 지난번처럼 아공간 포켓에 넣어 가야 해.」
204|
205|“그럼 됐어요. 바로 출발하시죠.”
206|
207|「그래, 그러자고. 진도 뭔가 알고 있는 것 같으니.」
208|
209|나와 매직 존슨이 막 발을 뗀 그때, 스켈레톤 킹이 점잖은 목소리로 끼어들었다.
210|
211|“듣던 중 미안하지만, 인간들이여. 이 몸은 긴한 용무가 있으니 너희끼리 가 보도록 하거라.”
212|
213|“……?”
214|
215|「……?」
216|
217|“호텔 프런트의 여직원이 매우 아름답더군. 비록 인간의 거죽에 가려져 있지만, 그 안에 숨겨진 골격의 곡선이 끝내줘.”
218|
219|나는 조용히 되물었다.
220|
221|“그래서?”
222|
223|“그래서는 무슨. 오늘은 외박할 것이니 그리 알고 있으라는 이야기지. 그럼 난 이만 미녀와의 약속을 잡으러…… 그런데 간악한 인간이여.”
224|
225|“왜?”
226|
227|“갑자기 창을 꺼낸 이유를 물어봐도 되겠나?”
228|
229|“아, 이거.”
230|
231|나는 어느새 인벤토리에서 꺼내든 백염을 슬쩍 흔들었다.
232|
233|“별거 아냐. 네가 돌아서면 찌르려고.”
234|
235|“음. 그렇군.”
236|
237|“그렇지.”
238|
239|“…….”
240|
241|“왜 안 가? 슬슬 직원들 퇴근할 시간인데. 빨리 가서 저녁 식사라도 하자고 꼬셔야지.”
242|
243|머뭇거리던 스켈레톤 킹의 입가에 어색한 미소가 맺혔다.
244|
245|“생각해 보니까 작업은 천천히 걸어도 될 것 같다.”
246|
247|“우와, 그럼 시간 비겠네. 그럼…….”
248|
249|나는 환하게 웃으며 사람들에게 인벤토리의 존재를 숨기기 위해 장만한 아공간 포켓 하나를 꺼내 들었다.
250|
251|“후딱 들어와, 새꺄.”
252|
253|“……으응.”
254|
255|시무룩하게 대답한 스켈레톤 킹이 아공간 포켓 안으로 모습을 쏙 감췄다.
256|
257|
258|
259|* * *
260|
261|
262|
263|마법진을 직접 눈으로 본 순간, 나는 스켈레톤 킹이 했던 말의 의미를 깨달을 수 있었다.
264|
265|아니, 어쩌면 녀석의 말을 들은 직후라 더 그렇게 느꼈는지도 모르겠다.
266|
267|하지만 보는 것과 동시에 압도되었고, 나도 모르게 한 가지 단어를 떠올렸다.
268|
269|‘죽음.’
270|
271|동굴에서 봤던 것과는 비교도 안 될 만큼 거대한 크기의 흑마법진.
272|
273|비록 마력이 끊기고 본래의 기능을 잃었다고는 하나, 한때 숱한 생명을 뺏었던 죽음의 흔적마저 사라지지는 않았다.
274|
275|그리고…… 그것이 내가 느낀 전부였다.
276|
277|「진. 어때? 뭔가 알 것 같아?」
278|
279|“아뇨. 전혀.”
280|
281|알 수 없는 순서, 배치로 이루어진 문양과 기호는 여전히 해석이 불가능했다.
282|
283|앞서 무림에서 그랬던 것처럼 시스템은 잠잠했고, 아무런 소득도 얻지 못한 나는 몇 시간이나 근처를 서성거리다가 발길을 돌릴 수밖에 없었다.
284|
285|“미스터 존슨, 그리고 진. 돌아가시는 길에 불편함이 없도록 경호를 준비했는데…….”
286|

[P79]
“Then how did you guess it was a life-force absorption circle? Can only monsters recognize patterns and symbols like these?”

[P80]
If the Skeleton King understood these strange patterns and symbols—if he could teach me what they meant—I might finally be able to identify the formation I had seen in Murim.

[P81]
I looked at him expectantly, only for his answer to dash my hopes a moment later.

[P82]
“I do not know what those things mean. I could determine the magic circle’s purpose only because I am undead.”

[P83]
The Skeleton King pointed at Magic Johnson and continued.

[P84]
“When I first saw it on paper, I could not tell what it was. But when I visited the site with that human I’m grateful to, I sensed it clearly. The stench of countless deaths hung over the place—more deaths than even I could begin to estimate. That was when I realized what it was.”

[P85]
“Oh…”

[P86]
I could not hide my disappointment.

[P87]
If neither Magic Johnson, a Grand Mage, nor the Skeleton King, a Named Monster, could understand them, then deciphering those patterns and symbols anytime soon would be practically impossible.

[P88]
*Damn it.*

[P89]
What the hell was going on?

[P90]
The formation carved into the center of the cave. The patterns and symbols in the magic circle discovered here. The bizarre phenomena I had witnessed during my battles with the Blood Lord and the Western Heaven Demon Lord…

[P91]
I desperately tried to deny the ominous thought that flashed through my mind.

[P92]
*That can’t be. It’s impossible.*

[P93]
Was this a coincidence? Or was it fate?

[P94]
And if it was fate, what did this connection that had suddenly appeared mean?

[P95]
After pacing silently around the suite for a long time, I abruptly spoke.

[P96]
“I need to see it for myself.”

[P97]
「Huh?」

[P98]
“Hmm?”

[P99]
“Johnson. I can visit the site that bastard went to, right?”

[P100]
Magic Johnson thought for a moment, then nodded.

[P101]
「It’s classified, but you should be able to get in, Jin. However, only the two of us can be seen. We’ll have to carry our friend in an extradimensional pocket, just like last time.」

[P102]
“That’s fine. Let’s leave right away.”

[P103]
「All right, let’s do that. You seem to know something too, Jin.」

[P104]
Just as Magic Johnson and I were about to leave, the Skeleton King cut in with a dignified voice.

[P105]
“I apologize for interrupting, humans, but this body has pressing business. You two may go without me.”

[P106]
“……?”

[P107]
「……?」

[P108]
“The woman at the hotel’s front desk is exceptionally beautiful. Though concealed beneath human skin, the curves of the skeleton within are exquisite.”

[P109]
I quietly asked,

[P110]
“So?”

[P111]
“What do you mean, ‘so’? I am informing you that I shall be spending the night out. Now, I must go arrange a date with the beauty… But, vile human.”

[P112]
“What?”

[P113]
“May I ask why you suddenly took out a spear?”

[P114]
“Ah, this?”

[P115]
I casually waved White Flame, which I had somehow already drawn from my Inventory.

[P116]
“It’s nothing. I was going to stab you when you turned around.”

[P117]
“I see.”

[P118]
“Exactly.”

[P119]
“……”

[P120]
“Why aren’t you leaving? The employees will be getting off work soon. You should hurry over and ask her to dinner.”

[P121]
The Skeleton King hesitated, an awkward smile tugging at his lips.

[P122]
“Now that I think about it, I suppose I can take my time trying to win her over.”

[P123]
“Wow, then you’ve got some free time. In that case…”

[P124]
I smiled brightly and pulled out one of the extradimensional pockets I had acquired to conceal the existence of my Inventory from other people.

[P125]
“Get in, asshole.”

[P126]
“……Okay.”

[P127]
The Skeleton King answered dejectedly and slipped inside the extradimensional pocket.

[P128]
* * *

[P129]
The moment I saw the magic circle with my own eyes, I understood what the Skeleton King had meant.

[P130]
Or perhaps I only felt that way because I had heard his explanation beforehand.

[P131]
Either way, the sight overwhelmed me, and a single word rose unbidden to my mind.

[P132]
*Death.*

[P133]
The enormous dark magic circle dwarfed the one I had seen in the cave.

[P134]
Its mana had been cut off, robbing it of its original function, but the traces of the countless lives it had once claimed had not disappeared.

[P135]
And… that was all I could sense.

[P136]
「Jin. What do you think? Do you have any idea what it is?」

[P137]
“No. None at all.”

[P138]
The patterns and symbols, arranged in an incomprehensible order, remained impossible to decipher.

[P139]
Just as it had in Murim, the System remained silent. After wandering around the site for hours without learning anything, I had no choice but to turn back.

[P140]
“Mr. Johnson, Jin. We’ve prepared an escort to ensure you encounter no inconvenience on your way back…”

[P141]
“We’re fine.”

[P142]
“Yes, sir. Then I hope we meet again.”

[P143]
We left the head of security and his guards behind after they snapped off razor-sharp salutes.

[P144]
Once he had made sure no one was nearby, Magic Johnson quietly moved his lips.

[P145]
「Jin. You knew something, didn’t you?」

[P146]
“…A dream. I think I saw something similar in a dream.”

[P147]
「Hmm.」

[P148]
“Johnson. Can I look around by myself for a while?”

[P149]
「Of course. How long do you think you’ll be?」

[P150]
“I’ll be back soon.”

[P151]
I began walking slowly through the ruins.

[P152]
Although it was well past midnight, the city was as bright as noon, and countless people and machines were working to clear the wreckage.

[P153]
The same work was probably underway in every city caught up in the war.

[P154]
*It must be the same in Sichuan.*

[P155]
China’s Sichuan and Murim’s Sichuan belonged to entirely different worlds. Murim was not the modern world’s past, nor was the modern world Murim’s future.

[P156]
But now a connection had appeared between those utterly different worlds—and it was not the first.

[P157]
*The capsule.*

[P158]
Everything that had happened to me had begun with the junk capsule I had picked up at a recycling center.

[P159]
*How? Why? For what reason?*

[P160]
More questions crowded my mind with every step, leaving my thoughts in complete disarray.

[P161]
“Phew.”

[P162]
At my deep sigh, the Skeleton King—whom I had quietly moved from the extradimensional pocket into my Inventory—asked,

[P163]
“Are you all right, vile human?”

[P164]
“Are you worried about me?”

[P165]
“No. If you are all right, let us hurry back to the hotel. Johnson told me a few days ago that there is a club nearby with a great crowd.”

[P166]
“……”

[P167]
*Give me back my touching moment, you lunatic.*

[P168]
I considered telling him that the club Johnson had mentioned was a gay bar, but held my tongue.

[P169]
“Forget it. What did I expect from you?”

[P170]
“So, when are we going back?”

[P171]
“I’m going, asshole. I said I’m going!”

[P172]
At that exact moment—

[P173]
“Where are you so desperate to go? Hell?”

[P174]
At the sound of the voice—harder and colder than ever before—I slowly turned around.

[P175]
I must have wandered deep into the ruins without realizing it. Beyond a relatively dark stretch of rubble, a familiar figure emerged through the wreckage of a collapsed building.

[P176]
“Hell is where your old man went. If I die, I’m going to heaven.”

[P177]
The eyes of Go Jun—Lee Jungryong’s Disciple and Head of Security—turned ice-cold.

Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. ### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.

[P136]
「Jin. What do you think? Do you have any idea what it is?」

[P137]
“No. None at all.”

[P138]
The patterns and symbols, arranged in an incomprehensible order, remained impossible to decipher.

[P139]
Just as it had in Murim, the System remained silent. After wandering around the site for hours without learning anything, I had no choice but to turn back.

[P140]
“Mr. Johnson, Jin. We’ve prepared an escort to ensure you encounter no inconvenience on your way back…”

[P141]
“We’re fine.”

[P142]
“Yes, sir. Then I hope we meet again.”

[P143]
We left the head of security and his guards behind after they snapped off razor-sharp salutes.

[P144]
Once he had made sure no one was nearby, Magic Johnson quietly moved his lips.

[P145]
「Jin. You knew something, didn’t you?」

[P146]
“…A dream. I think I saw something similar in a dream.”

[P147]
「Hmm.」

[P148]
“Johnson. Can I look around by myself for a while?”

[P149]
「Of course. How long do you think you’ll be?」

[P150]
“I’ll be back soon.”

[P151]
I began walking slowly through the ruins.

[P152]
Although it was well past midnight, the city was as bright as noon, and countless people and machines were working to clear the wreckage.

[P153]
The same work was probably underway in every city caught up in the war.

[P154]
*It must be the same in Sichuan.*

[P155]
China’s Sichuan and Murim’s Sichuan belonged to entirely different worlds. Murim was not the modern world’s past, nor was the modern world Murim’s future.

[P156]
But now a connection had appeared between those utterly different worlds—and it was not the first.

[P157]
*The capsule.*

[P158]
Everything that had happened to me had begun with the junk capsule I had picked up at a recycling center.

[P159]
*How? Why? For what reason?*

[P160]
More questions crowded my mind with every step, leaving my thoughts in complete disarray.

[P161]
“Phew.”

[P162]
At my deep sigh, the Skeleton King—whom I had quietly moved from the extradimensional pocket into my Inventory—asked,

[P163]
“Are you all right, vile human?”

[P164]
“Are you worried about me?”

[P165]
“No. If you are all right, let us hurry back to the hotel. Johnson told me a few days ago that there is a club nearby with a great crowd.”

[P166]
“……”

[P167]
*Give me back my touching moment, you lunatic.*

[P168]
I considered telling him that the club Johnson had mentioned was a gay bar, but held my tongue.

[P169]
“Forget it. What did I expect from you?”

[P170]
“So, when are we going back?”

[P171]
“I’m going, asshole. I said I’m going!”

[P172]
At that exact moment—

[P173]
“Where are you so desperate to go? Hell?”

[P174]
At the sound of the voice—harder and colder than ever before—I slowly turned around.

[P175]
I must have wandered deep into the ruins without realizing it. Beyond a relatively dark stretch of rubble, a familiar figure emerged through the wreckage of a collapsed building.

[P176]
“Hell is where your old man went. If I die, I’m going to heaven.”

[P177]
The eyes of Go Jun—Lee Jungryong’s Disciple and Head of Security—turned ice-cold.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 430

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃430화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|나도 모르게 눈꺼풀이 파르르 떨렸다.
  6|
  7|‘……이게 왜 여기에.’
  8|
  9|똑똑히 기억하고 있다.
 10|
 11|서천마군에 의해 몇 번이나 죽을 위기를 넘겨야 했던 사천혈사(四川血史)가 마무리된 직후, 청성파와 아미파 장문인의 인도하에 향했던 어느 이름 모를 절벽의 동굴.
 12|
 13|기문진 뒤에 숨겨져 있던 공간은 실로 광활했고, 그 중심부에는 거대한 진법(陳法)이 새겨져 있었다.
 14|
 15|지금 내가 들고 있는 종이에 컬러로 프린트된, 기이한 문양과 기호로 가득한 진법이.
 16|
 17|하지만…… 청성과 아미의 장문인들이 이동진(異動陳)이라 이름 붙였던 그것을 더 이상 진법이라고 부를 수 있을까?
 18|
 19|나는 다급히 매직 존슨을 향해 종이를 들이밀었다.
 20|
 21|“존슨. 이거, 이거 뭐예요?”
 22|
 23|「어, 어?」
 24|
 25|“이게 왜…… 아니, 도대체 어디서 난 겁니까?”
 26|
 27|갑작스러운 내 반응에 당황한 매직 존슨이 얼떨떨한 표정으로 대꾸했다.
 28|
 29|「아크 리치가 본거지로 삼았던 도시에서 발견한 마법진이야.」
 30|
 31|“마법진이요?”
 32|
 33|「응, 마법진. 안 그래도 이것 때문에 한창 연구 중이었는데…… 왜 그래, 진? 혹시 어디서 본 적 있어?」
 34|
 35|“다른 것도 있어요?”
 36|
 37|「물론이지. 네가 들어오기 전까지 보고 있던 종이들이 전부 그것과 관련된 내용이니까.」
 38|
 39|“네?”
 40|
 41|그럼 책상 위에 쌓여 있던 그게 전부?
 42|
 43|나는 바닥에 널브러진 수십여 장의 종이를 바라보았다.
 44|
 45|“자, 잠깐만 실례할게요.”
 46|
 47|「진, 진?」
 48|
 49|“드디어 미쳐 버린 것인가. 안타깝구나, 못생기고 간악한 인간이여.”
 50|
 51|당황한 매직 존슨의 부름과 스켈레톤 킹의 헛소리는 안중에도 없었다.
 52|
 53|나는 입을 꾹 다문 채 프린트된 종이 뭉치를 빠르게 훑어 나갔다.
 54|
 55|수십 장의 종이에는 각각의 문양과 기호가 새겨져 있었고, 그 모든 것을 다 살펴본 후 한 가지 사실을 깨달을 수 있었다.
 56|
 57|‘이건…….’
 58|
 59|틀림없다. 배치와 방향이 다를 뿐, 기이한 문양과 기호는 무림에서 본 그것과 동일했다.
 60|
 61|그리고 이 종이들을 퍼즐처럼 한데 모으면 하나의 거대한 마법진이 완성된다는 것도.
 62|
 63|‘이게 무슨 개 같은 상황이지?’
 64|
 65|쇠망치로 뒤통수를 한 대 얻어맞은 기분이다.
 66|
 67|말없이 종이들을 노려보던 내가 입을 연 것은 그로부터 상당한 시간이 흐른 뒤였다.
 68|
 69|“이거, 아크 리치의 본거지에서 발견한 거라고 하셨죠?”
 70|
 71|어느새 시가를 문 매직 존슨을 바라보며 묻자, 그가 연기를 뿜으며 대답했다.
 72|
 73|「그래. 나도 처음에는 그런 게 있는 줄 몰랐는데, 조사단 투입 직후에 발견된 것 같아. 이틀째에 연합군을 통해서 전달받았지.」
 74|
 75|“전달받았다는 건…….”
 76|
 77|「내게 자문을 구했거든. 저쪽에서도 정확히 어떤 기능의 마법진인지 파악하지 못한 거지. 아마 나 말고 다른 두 명에게도 연락이 갔을걸?」
 78|
 79|다른 두 명이란 매직 존슨을 제외한 다른 대마도사들일 것이다. 그들이야말로 현존하는 최고의 마법사들이자, 진정한 전문가들이니까.
 80|
 81|그리고 그 말은 이 마법진이 지금껏 드러난 적 없는 새로운 종류의 것이라는 뜻이기도 했다.
 82|
 83|“그래서, 연구하신 결과는 나왔습니까?”
 84|
 85|「아직 정확한 건 아니지만, 마법진의 용도에 대해서는 갈피를 잡았지.」
 86|
 87|“용도요?”
 88|
 89|「응. 다행히 그쪽에 대해 제법 잘 아는 친구가 하나 있었거든.」
 90|
 91|그게 누구냐고 물어보려던 순간, 한 사람이 오만한 목소리로 불쑥 끼어들었다.
 92|
 93|“바로 이 몸이시지. 미국 조지아주 애틀랜타에서 출생한 우주 대존잘 미남. 이름하여 스톤-킹.”
 94|
 95|맞다. 왜 저놈을 잊고 있었지?
 96|
 97|마계 토박이에 네임드 몬스터씩이나 되는 놈이니 뭔가를 알고 있을 것이 분명하다.
 98|
 99|나는 헛소리를 늘어놓는 스켈레톤 킹을 다그쳤다.
100|
101|“개소리하지 말고 아는 거나 빨리 털어놔.”
102|

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
